reason: Copying the nuclear DNA is essential to giving each daughter cell a complete genome.
expectation: The nucleotides should be used to replicate the cell's existing DNA; I am unsure how the resulting chromosomes will be represented.

alternatives.reason: A spindle will also be needed, but copying the DNA first seems a natural starting point.

effect: DNA is copied into sister chromatids; the next goal requires a spindle and a grown cell.
reaction: The old-and-new strand depiction makes replication clear.
reason: Build the spindle needed to separate the copied chromosomes.
expectation: The proteins and duplicated centrosomes will form a chromosome-moving spindle.

alternatives.reason: New membrane is also needed for growth, but the spindle directly addresses the newly revealed goal.

effect: The spindle is assembled as a mitosis preview, but needs the grown cell before it can act on chromosomes.
reaction: The timing caption helps distinguish the preview from chromosome separation.
reason: Prepare new membrane for cell growth; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The phospholipids and proteins will form new membrane material for the growing cell.

effect: The membrane supply is packaged into vesicles routed through the ER and Golgi; it can now enlarge the copied-DNA cell.
reaction: The delivery pathway makes the connection to membrane growth clearer.
reason: Enlarge the cell using the membrane supply; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The vesicles will add membrane to the cell, producing a grown cell ready for spindle action.

effect: The cell has grown and retains its copied DNA, so it is ready for spindle action.
reaction: The labels make the completed preparations easy to follow.
reason: Use the spindle to separate the copied chromosomes; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The spindle will move sister chromatids apart and form two daughter nuclei.

effect: The spindle separated the sister copies into two nuclei, but the cytoplasm remains connected and must divide.
reaction: The time strip clearly distinguishes nuclear separation from division of the cell.
reason: Use actin and myosin to divide the cytoplasm; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the furrow and separate the cell into two daughters.

effect: Cytoplasmic division produced two separate stem cells with complete genomes, completing the chapter; differentiation is shown as a later possibility.
reaction: The final picture connects cell division to self-renewal, though it does not show how actin and myosin constrict the cell.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle to separate the copied chromosomes was most worthwhile: the planned time strip distinguishes formation of two nuclei from division of the cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Enlarging the cell was a relatively uneventful, only-offered step; its result mainly confirmed preparations already made.

surprise.text: The spindle construction was explicitly presented as a preview of assembly during mitosis, rather than an immediate event inside the cell.

arbitrary.text: The compatible action to make a spindle from generic new cell proteins and centrosomes made sense in outline, but tubulin first appeared in the result, so that specific connection was not clear beforehand.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the daughter cells become different tissue types. The chapter made the sequence understandable, though several choices were forced.
